declared_learner_decisions.statement: Classify a suspected acute coronary syndrome from the ischemic presentation, the electrocardiogram and troponin.
Choose the reperfusion strategy for a diagnostic ST-elevation infarct presenting to a centre without percutaneous capability.
Recognise which mechanical complication explains new haemodynamic deterioration after a myocardial infarct.
Stabilise hypotension arising from right-ventricular infarct physiology.
Choose the next investigation when acute coronary syndrome remains suspected after a non-diagnostic initial electrocardiogram and a non-elevated initial high-sensitivity troponin.
Decide the level of care for a patient whose troponin trajectory and electrocardiogram meet the high-risk criteria of a non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome.
Recognise the diagnosis in an adult presenting with right lower quadrant pain.
Select the imaging study when clinical probability is intermediate.
Choose operative versus non-operative management for a complicated presentation.
Decide the disposition when imaging is non-diagnostic and suspicion on reassessment remains intermediate.
Diagnose which entity on the inflammatory spectrum a presentation represents.
Choose the investigation that characterises a residual area after treatment.
Advise on milk removal from the affected side during treatment.
Recognise which entity a worsening firm mass-like area without fluctuance represents.
Decide whether an inflammatory breast presentation requires hospital admission and intravenous therapy.
Choose the definitive step once a fluid collection has been demonstrated.
Diagnose the illness from a first wheezing episode following a viral prodrome.
Choose the level of monitoring for an infant admitted with this illness.
Choose the ceiling of supportive care for worsening work of breathing.
Decide whether an admitted infant meets the criteria for discharge.
Choose the route of supplemental hydration when the respiratory rate makes oral feeding unsafe.
Identify which measurement artefact explains an observed screening result.
Choose the revision to an invitation letter that best protects autonomy.
Decide the programme action required before invitations are issued.
Decide what the screening interval of a proposed programme should be based on.
Identify which harm of screening a described programme outcome represents.
Separate the depressive diagnoses across a longitudinal course.
Decide the disposition for a patient presenting with acute suicide risk.
Choose the initial treatment by severity and safety risk.
Decide which baseline investigations to order at the time of diagnosis.
Choose the initial treatment when the patient declines pharmacotherapy and in-person structured psychotherapy is unavailable.
Choose the initial treatment for a severe depressive episode with psychotic features.

authorship: The G1 declaration is carried forward verbatim and additional decisions were enumerated from the same admitted evidence packets and the same MCC objectives BEFORE any G2 scenario was written. Like the G1 declaration this is pilot-scoped: it is not the canonical per-address authoring task, which remains open and needs its own authorisation.
